examples.en: The two countries are cooperating closely.
The team members work while keeping in close contact.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 관계 기관과 긴밀히 상의해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to consult closely with the related agencies on this issue.
I'm contacting you because I have something to discuss in confidence.
The police are working in close coordination with the school.
If departments communicate closely, mistakes decrease.

explain: 협력하다, 연락하다, 소통하다, 상의하다처럼 서로 주고받는 동작과 같이 써요. '가깝게'보다 격식 있어서 업무, 뉴스, 공식적인 말에서 많이 나와요. 형용사 '긴밀하다'는 '긴밀한 관계'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs of exchange such as 협력하다 (cooperate), 연락하다 (contact), 소통하다 (communicate) and 상의하다 (consult). It is more formal than '가깝게' and is common in work, news and official talk. The adjective '긴밀하다' is used as in '긴밀한 관계'.

en: important and trivial matters; all sorts of occasions

examples.en: My eldest brother takes care of family affairs.

examples.ko: 부모님은 동네 대소사에 빠지지 않고 참석하세요.
examples.en: My parents never miss neighborhood events.

examples.ko: 새로 온 팀장님이 회사 대소사를 꼼꼼히 챙겨요.
examples.en: The new team leader carefully looks after all the company's matters.
I'm busy every weekend because of relatives' events.

examples.ko: 집안의 대소사가 있을 때마다 온 가족이 모여요.
examples.en: The whole family gathers whenever there's a family occasion.

examples.ko: 결혼이나 장례 같은 대소사에는 꼭 인사를 가야 해요.
examples.en: You must go to pay your respects at occasions like weddings and funerals.

explain: 크고 작은 일을 뜻하고, 특히 결혼·장례·돌잔치 같은 집안이나 모임의 행사를 말할 때 많이 써요. '집안 대소사'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 일상 대화보다는 어른들의 말이나 글에서 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It means matters big and small, and is often used for events like weddings, funerals, and first-birthday parties in a family or group. '집안 대소사' is the most natural pairing. It shows up more in adults' speech and writing than in everyday chat.

examples.en: A person from HR also sat in on the interview.
May I join you at dinner?

examples.ko: 회의에 변호사가 동석하면 더 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: It's more reassuring if a lawyer is present at the meeting.

examples.ko: 그 자리에 동석한 분들이 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Everyone who was at that table applauded.
Do you want your parents to be present at the counseling?
I had something to do, so I couldn't join them.

explain: 같은 '자리'에 함께 앉아 있다는 뜻이 중심이라 식사, 회의, 상담 같은 자리에 써요. 식당에서 모르는 사람과 같은 테이블을 쓰는 것은 '합석하다'라고 해요. 탈것을 같이 타는 '동승하다'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: The core idea is being together at the same seat or gathering, so it fits meals, meetings and consultations. Sharing a table with strangers at a restaurant is '합석하다'. Don't confuse it with '동승하다', which is about riding in the same vehicle.

en: each and every one; all faces

examples.ko: 이번 대표팀의 면면을 보면 우승이 기대돼요.
examples.en: Looking at the lineup of this national team, I expect them to win.
The people who attended were really impressive.
The members of the committee have not been made public yet.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들의 면면을 떠올리면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: Thinking of each of my classmates makes me smile.

examples.ko: 이 모임의 면면 하나하나가 다 전문가예요.
examples.en: Every single member of this group is an expert.
It's a movie I'm excited for just from seeing the cast.

explain: 여러 사람의 얼굴이나 구성원을 하나하나 가리킬 때 써요. 보통 '대표팀의 면면', '출연진의 면면'처럼 사람 모음 뒤에 붙이고 한 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. '면면히'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It points to the faces or members of a group one by one. It usually follows a group, as in '대표팀의 면면' (the lineup of the national team) or '출연진의 면면' (the cast), and is not used for a single person. It is a different word from '면면히', so don't mix them up.

examples.en: Please keep private chatting to a minimum during the meeting.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 친구와 사담을 나누다가 혼났어요.
examples.en: I got scolded for chatting with a friend during class.

examples.ko: 사담이지만 저는 이 계획이 좀 걱정돼요.
examples.en: This is just between us, but I am a bit worried about this plan.
Can I have a quick private word?

examples.ko: 두 사람은 회의가 끝난 뒤에도 사담을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: The two kept talking privately even after the meeting ended.
The private chat went on too long, so the meeting started late.

explain: 회의나 수업, 일하는 자리에서 업무와 상관없는 개인적인 이야기를 가리켜요. '잡담'과 비슷하지만 '사담'은 공적인 자리와 대비해서 쓰는 느낌이 있어요. '사담이지만'은 이야기를 꺼낼 때 앞에 붙이는 말로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to personal talk unrelated to work in a meeting, class or workplace. It is close to '잡담' (idle chat), but '사담' carries a contrast with the formal setting. '사담이지만' is also used as an opener like 'this is off the record'.

examples.en: My friend suggested that we travel together.

examples.ko: 회사가 저에게 팀장 자리를 제의해 왔어요.
examples.en: The company has offered me a team leader position.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 경기 날짜를 바꾸자고 제의했는데 거절했어요.
examples.en: The other team proposed changing the match date, but we declined.

examples.ko: 제의하는 사람이 먼저 조건을 설명해야 해요.
examples.en: The person making the offer should explain the terms first.

examples.ko: 그에게 먼저 화해를 제의할까 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm wondering whether to offer to make up with him first.
Everyone agreed to the plan he proposed.

explain: 제의하다는 상대에게 어떤 일을 해 보자고 의견이나 안을 내놓을 때 써요. '제안하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '같이 하자고 했어요'처럼 쉬운 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: 제의하다 is for putting an idea or proposal to someone, such as suggesting they do something together. It is close to 제안하다 in meaning. In daily talk people often just say 같이 하자고 했어요.

examples.en: There are four members in our group.
I made the presentation materials with my group members.

examples.ko: 조원 중에 한 명이 아파서 결석했어요.
examples.en: One of the group members was sick and absent.
The group members gathered and divided up the roles.
A new member joined and brightened the mood.

examples.ko: 저희 조원은 모두 열심히 해서 고마워요.
examples.en: I'm grateful that everyone in our group worked hard.

explain: 학교 수업이나 모임에서 여럿이 한 '조'로 묶일 때 그 안의 사람이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '팀원'도 쓰는데 학교에서는 '조원', 회사나 운동에서는 '팀원'이 더 자연스러워요. 숫자 뒤의 '조 원'(trillion won)과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is a person in a 조 (group) formed in class or a gathering. 팀원 is similar, but 조원 sounds natural at school and 팀원 at work or in sports. It is unrelated to '조 원' (trillion won) after a number.
